Local security tunnel, not a remote VPN

GeDefense creates an on-device VPN interface so traffic can pass through the local GaiaNet security engine. Traffic is not forwarded to a VisionGaiaTechnology VPN server. The purpose is firewall, threat-intelligence and XDR enforcement on this device.

To enforce policy, GeDefense may process destination IP addresses, DNS domain names, protocol and port metadata, flow counters and app/UID attribution when Android exposes it. This data is used for local security decisions and local security views.
No payload decryption or advertising telemetry

GeDefense does not perform TLS or QUIC interception, does not decrypt application payloads, has no advertising or analytics SDK, and does not upload observed destination IPs, DNS queries, package inventory or traffic history to VisionGaiaTechnology.

GeDefense has no account requirement, advertising SDK or analytics SDK. Security state, findings, policy, traffic analytics and scanner results are stored locally. Authenticated state stores reject tampered snapshots instead of silently trusting them.

The Android VpnService routes device traffic through the local GaiaNet engine for firewall and threat-intelligence enforcement. Destination IP, DNS name, protocol, port, byte/flow counters and app attribution may be processed locally. GeDefense does not decrypt TLS/QUIC payloads and does not send observed traffic history to a VGT backend.

Installed-app metadata, signer/permission information, APK hashes and user-selected or shared-storage file metadata may be processed locally for malware and integrity analysis. Broad file access is used only for the local antivirus scanner. Files are not uploaded, executed, modified or deleted by the scanner.

Package visibility supports antivirus/XDR inventory and signer drift detection. Usage access supports local traffic attribution. Coarse location is optional, reads only last-known network/passive fixes, is quantized before use and has no background tracking subscription. Device-admin or Device-Owner capabilities are used only when TITAN is explicitly provisioned.

Support export is started by the user through Android’s document picker. The aggregate-only bundle excludes package names, app labels, IP addresses, domains, file paths, signer/APK hashes, packet/evidence payloads and XDR incident detail text.

This assistant explains each special access before you open Android settings. Optional access is marked as optional. You can finish setup without enabling the scanner, usage access, location or TITAN.
Defense in depth, not one magic switch

GeDefense combines independent controls so that one missed indicator does not automatically become a missed incident. Network enforcement, app analysis, integrity checks, behavior signals and XDR correlation remain separate modules with bounded authority.
Evidence gets stronger when signals agree

A suspicious permission, an unusual connection or a heuristic file match can be noisy alone. GeDefense raises confidence when independent evidence points to the same package, destination or event and preserves the underlying reasons for review.

GeDefense reduces attack surface and improves visibility; it cannot prove that every file, app or connection is harmless. Android sandbox boundaries, OEM behavior and new threats still matter. High-impact findings should be reviewed with their evidence.

Core network protection uses Android VpnService as a local traffic interface. GaiaNet evaluates flows, firewall policy and threat-intelligence matches on the device. Android will separately ask for system VPN permission when protection is activated.
No commercial remote VPN tunnel: GeDefense does not route your traffic through a VisionGaiaTechnology VPN server.
No TLS interception: GeDefense does not install a root certificate or decrypt encrypted HTTPS content.
No traffic-history upload: observed destination and flow history is not uploaded to VisionGaiaTechnology.
Why Android shows the VPN icon

Android reserves the VpnService interface for apps that inspect or route traffic. The system VPN indicator therefore shows that GeDefense owns the local traffic interface; it does not mean your traffic is being sent to a remote VPN provider.
Threat intelligence is one source of evidence

GeDefense downloads curated malicious-IP and network feeds over HTTPS and compiles them into local policy data. Feed authority is bounded: some sources can block, while others only correlate or annotate.

After you finish this setup, XDR may enumerate installed packages, signer information and relevant permissions to establish a local security baseline. Package inventory is not uploaded to VisionGaiaTechnology.

GeDefense keeps the reason behind a finding so you can distinguish a heuristic signal from stronger correlated or blocking evidence. The goal is explainable response, not a dramatic red screen for every anomaly.
All-files access expands scanning to shared storage such as Downloads, documents, APK archives and removable media.

GeDefense does not request fine or background location and does not start continuous location updates. The atlas uses a quantized coarse origin locally and can operate without this permission.

While Full Flow is active, GaiaNet blocks known advertising, analytics and optional device-telemetry endpoints locally before traffic leaves the device. Decisions come from the signed local Privacy Intelligence snapshot; GeDefense does not query a VGT cloud or third-party telemetry service for verdicts.
What Telemetry Shield deliberately does and does not do
System-wide telemetry filtering requires Full Flow. Selective mode does not claim complete telemetry protection.
No TLS interception: HTTPS content stays encrypted. Unknown DoH over shared HTTPS/443, hard-coded resolver IPs or ECH can remain outside domain visibility.
Conservative is enabled by default; Balanced, Strict and Off remain user-selectable in the Privacy Center. Essential connectivity, push and update services take precedence over blocking rules.

There is no advertising SDK or behavioral analytics SDK in the Android app.
Diagnostics are aggregate-only and are exported only when you explicitly choose a destination; GeDefense does not silently upload support bundles.
The Privacy Center documents local processing, scanner scope, network services and VPN consent. VPN consent can also be revoked there, which stops VPN protection.

Sensitive local state is protected with domain-separated AES-256-GCM keys in Android Keystore, an independent HMAC-SHA-256 layer, versioned key rotation and encrypted evidence records. StrongBox is preferred when the device can satisfy the requested key profile; otherwise Android hardware-backed Keystore is used when available.
